property_summary: After calling Collect with any amount, MinSum remains unchanged (equal to the initial value set before initialization).
After Collect is called and reverts, MinSum stays equal to the value set by SetMinSum before initialization.
After Collect is called with any amount (regardless of revert), MinSum retains the value set by the last SetMinSum call before initialization.
After Collect is called (whether it reverts or not), MinSum equals the value set by the last call to SetMinSum before initialization.
After a call to Collect that succeeds (does not revert), the value of MinSum must equal the value set by the last SetMinSum call before initialization.
MinSum remains unchanged after Collect() is called, unless Collect() is called with a non-zero amount and the caller's balance exceeds MinSum.
After a call to Collect(uint256), state variable MinSum retains the value set during initialization.
After any call to Collect(uint256), MinSum equals the value set by SetMinSum(uint256) during initialization.
After any call to Collect(uint256), MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After any call to Collect(uint256), MinSum remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After calling Collect with any amount, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its initial value.
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable must be set to the same value it had at the start of the call, which is true only if SetMinSum can revert (preventing modification).
The value of MinSum before any call to Collect equals the value after the call, ensuring SetMinSum cannot be called after initialization.
The MinSum state variable is unchanged after any call to Collect, which holds only if SetMinSum can revert.
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable equals the value set during setUp (which is 0), because SetMinSum reverts after initialization.
After a Collect call, the LogFile address equals the address passed to SetLogFile (or is unchanged if SetLogFile was never called).
After a Collect call, the stored LogFile address is non-zero if SetLogFile was called with a non-zero address before initialization.

After a Collect call, the value of LogFile (as obtained through the generated getter c.LogFile()) is always equal to the last address that was passed to SetLogFile before initialization, or the zero address if SetLogFile was never called.
After a Collect call, the LogFile address is always the address that was passed to SetLogFile (or zero if never called).
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the LogFile address should match the last value provided by SetLogFile (or zero if never called), unless initialization was skipped.
After Collect(uint256), the caller's balance in Acc remains non-negative and the contract's balance decreases by exactly the collected amount.
After Collect, the caller's Acc.balance plus the collected amount equals the caller's Acc.balance before Collect.
After Collect(uint256) returns without revert, the caller's Acc.balance is exactly the caller's previous Acc.balance minus the collected amount.

After Collect(uint256) reverts, the caller's Acc.balance in the reference C remains unchanged from before the call, whereas in the mutant it may change due to a prior Put invocation within the same transaction.

After a successful Collect call, the total balance in the contract (sum of all Acc balances plus contract balance) is equal to the sum before the call minus the collected amount in the reference, but not in the mutant.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract decreases exactly by the amount collected (acc.balance = old_balance - _am).
For any account with enough balance and after the unlock time, a successful Collect call will result in the LogFile's History length increasing by exactly one entry recording the Collect event.
The number of LogFile.History entries after a Collect call from a given caller equals the number of successful Put calls from that caller.
After any Collect call, the LogFile's History length is at least as large as it was before the call.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's MinSum state variable remains unchanged.
After Collect, the sum of all balances in Acc plus c's own balance equals total incoming ether minus total collected ether.
After Collect, the balance of the caller should decrease exactly by the amount collected when the collect succeeds.
After a Collect call, the unlock time of the caller is never less than the sum of the old unlock time and the lock duration from the last Put.
After a Collect call, the unlock time of the caller is not updated when the caller never called Put (i.e., the mapping Holder's unlockTime remains 0).

After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the unlock time of the caller must be greater than the current block timestamp by the lock duration added in the most recent Put call, adjusted for any lock time already set.
Collect should revert when block.timestamp equals unlockTime
Collect must revert when block.timestamp equals unlockTime
Collect should not increase the caller's balance when block.timestamp equals unlockTime
When block.timestamp equals unlockTime, Collect does not change the contract's MinSum value.
Collect(uint256 _am) must revert when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime and acc.balance >= MinSum and acc.balance >= _am.
The caller's balance after Collect must be decreased by the full requested amount _am.
The condition for Collect to succeed (not revert) requires acc.balance >= _am in reference, but mutant requires acc.balance > _am, breaking when balance equals _am.
After a successful Collect, the caller's Ether balance increases by exactly _am, but the contract's total ether balance decreases by exactly _am.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the contract's total Ether balance never decreases by less than the sum of all successfully collected amounts.
After a successful Collect call (not reverting), the contract's MinSum remains unchanged.
Collect succeeds only if acc.balance >= MinSum
Collect can only reduce balance when acc.balance > MinSum (strictly greater), not when equal.
Collect can lower caller's balance to below MinSum when balance equals MinSum, but not when balance > MinSum.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance never becomes exactly equal to MinSum when it started equal to MinSum.
When the caller's balance equals MinSum, Collect must be able to reduce it to zero.
